title: Design Secure REST API
question: Design secure REST API for banking application. Requirements: 1) Public and authenticated endpoints, 2) Protect against common attacks (SQL injection, XSS, CSRF), 3) Rate limiting to prevent abuse, 4) Secure authentication and authorization, 5) API key management for third-party integrations, 6) Audit logging for compliance, 7) Handle sensitive data (account numbers, transactions). Discuss: using Spring Security for authentication with JWT tokens, implementing OAuth 2.0 for third-party access, using @PreAuthorize for method-level authorization, implementing role-based access control (RBAC) with user roles (CUSTOMER, TELLER, ADMIN), using prepared statements and JPA to prevent SQL injection, implementing input validation with Bean Validation annotations (@NotNull, @Pattern, @Size), sanitizing and encoding output to prevent XSS, using Content Security Policy headers, implementing CSRF protection with CSRF tokens for state-changing operations, using SameSite cookie attribute, implementing rate limiting with Bucket4j or Redis-based rate limiter (e.g., 100 requests per minute per user), using API Gateway for global rate limiting, implementing API key authentication for partners with expiring keys, storing API keys hashed in database, implementing request/response logging with sensitive data masking (mask account numbers showing last 4 digits, mask amounts in logs), using structured audit logging for all transactions, implementing HTTPS with TLS 1.2+, using secure headers (Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options), implementing input validation for file uploads (type, size, content validation), using parameterized queries for dynamic SQL, implementing defense in depth with multiple security layers, using security scanning tools (OWASP Dependency Check, Snyk) in CI/CD pipeline, implementing error handling that doesn't expose internal details, and using least privilege principle for database access.

title: Prevent and Detect Data Breaches
question: Implement security measures to prevent and detect data breaches in e-commerce application. Requirements: 1) Store customer PII (names, addresses, payment info), 2) Comply with PCI-DSS for payment data, 3) Detect unauthorized access attempts, 4) Implement data encryption, 5) Monitor suspicious activities, 6) Incident response plan, 7) Handle 1M customers. Discuss: implementing encryption at rest using AES-256 for sensitive data in database, using Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) at database level, encrypting backups, implementing encryption in transit with HTTPS/TLS for all communications, using certificate pinning for mobile apps, storing passwords with BCrypt (cost factor 12+), never storing plain passwords or reversible encryption, tokenizing payment card data using payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal) to avoid storing card numbers, implementing PCI-DSS compliant environment with network segmentation, using separate database for payment data with restricted access, implementing field-level encryption for PII columns, using database views to restrict access to sensitive columns, implementing role-based access control with principle of least privilege, using database audit logging for all access to sensitive tables, implementing anomaly detection for unusual data access patterns (large data exports, after-hours access, access from unusual locations), using SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) tool to aggregate logs and detect patterns, implementing alerting for suspicious activities (multiple failed login attempts, privilege escalation attempts, bulk data queries), using Web Application Firewall (WAF) to detect and block attacks, implementing intrusion detection system (IDS), using database activity monitoring (DAM), implementing data loss prevention (DLP) tools to detect sensitive data exfiltration, implementing incident response plan with defined roles and procedures, using security testing (penetration testing, vulnerability scanning) regularly, implementing secure coding practices and security training for developers, using dependency scanning to detect vulnerable libraries, and conducting regular security audits.

title: Secure File Upload System
question: Design secure file upload system for document management application. Requirements: 1) Allow PDF, DOCX, images upload, 2) Prevent malware upload, 3) Prevent path traversal attacks, 4) Limit file size and prevent DoS, 5) Scan uploaded files, 6) Store securely, 7) Control access to uploaded files. Discuss: implementing whitelist of allowed file extensions and MIME types, validating file content (magic numbers) not just extension to prevent disguised malicious files, implementing file size limits (e.g., 10MB per file, 100MB per user), using virus scanning with ClamAV or third-party service (VirusTotal API) on upload, quarantining suspicious files for manual review, generating random UUIDs for filenames to prevent path traversal and information disclosure, storing files outside web root or in object storage (S3) with private access, never executing or serving uploaded files from application directory, implementing path sanitization to remove '../' sequences, using content-disposition header with 'attachment' to force download instead of inline display, scanning for embedded scripts in documents, implementing content security policy to prevent XSS from uploaded HTML files, using separate domain for serving user content to isolate from main application domain, implementing access control to verify user owns or has permission for file before serving, generating time-limited signed URLs for file access, logging all file operations (upload, download, delete) with user information, implementing rate limiting on file uploads to prevent abuse, using chunked upload for large files with validation on each chunk, implementing file type detection libraries (Apache Tika) to verify actual file type, storing file metadata (original name, size, type, upload time, uploader) in database, implementing antivirus signature updates, using image processing libraries to strip metadata and sanitize images, and implementing backup and retention policies for uploaded files.

title: Secure Password Reset Flow
question: Implement secure password reset functionality. Requirements: 1) Email-based password reset, 2) Prevent account enumeration, 3) Prevent token reuse, 4) Time-limited tokens, 5) Secure token generation, 6) Rate limiting to prevent abuse, 7) Audit logging. Discuss: generating cryptographically secure random tokens using SecureRandom (at least 256 bits), storing hashed tokens in database (using SHA-256 or similar), never storing plain tokens, setting token expiration (15-30 minutes), invalidating token after single use, storing user ID with token to prevent token guessing, implementing same response time for valid and invalid email addresses to prevent account enumeration ('If account exists, email has been sent'), using generic error messages ('Reset link sent if account exists'), implementing rate limiting on reset requests (e.g., max 3 requests per hour per email), using CAPTCHA after multiple failed attempts, sending reset link via email with HTTPS link containing token as query parameter, not sending new password via email, implementing new password complexity requirements (minimum length, character types), forcing user to provide new password that's different from old ones, implementing session invalidation for all existing sessions after password reset, logging all password reset attempts (initiated, completed, failed) with timestamps and IP addresses, sending notification email to user when password is changed, implementing security questions as additional factor (optional but less secure), using account lockout after multiple failed reset attempts, implementing email verification before allowing reset for added security, and displaying last password change date to user on login.

title: Multi-Tenant Application Security
question: Implement security in multi-tenant SaaS application. Requirements: 1) Complete data isolation between tenants, 2) Prevent cross-tenant data access, 3) Tenant-specific configurations, 4) Shared infrastructure, 5) Performance at scale (1000 tenants), 6) Compliance with data residency requirements. Discuss: implementing tenant identification strategy using subdomain (tenant1.app.com) or path-based (/tenant1) routing, storing tenant ID in JWT token or session after authentication, using tenant context holder (ThreadLocal) to propagate tenant ID through request, implementing database-level isolation strategies: separate database per tenant (highest isolation, complex management), separate schema per tenant (good isolation, easier management), or shared schema with tenant_id column (least isolation, best performance), implementing row-level security with tenant_id in all queries, using JPA filters or Hibernate filters to automatically add tenant_id to queries, implementing query interceptors to verify tenant_id in all queries, preventing global admin queries from accidentally accessing wrong tenant data, implementing separate cache per tenant to prevent data leakage, using cache keys with tenant prefix (tenant1:user:123), implementing tenant-aware audit logging, using separate object storage folders per tenant, implementing tenant-specific encryption keys for data at rest, using tenant context in all service methods, implementing aspect to verify tenant authorization before method execution, preventing horizontal privilege escalation by validating tenant ownership, implementing integration tests that verify tenant isolation, using database views or stored procedures that enforce tenant filtering, implementing tenant-specific configuration (themes, features, limits), using feature flags per tenant, implementing data residency by deploying tenant data in specific regions, implementing tenant provisioning and deprovisioning workflows, using tenant migration tools for upgrades, and implementing monitoring and alerting per tenant for usage and security events.
